card.title: Metal ions in life — Mg in leaves, Fe in blood

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Life runs on metal ions: bulk Na⁺/K⁺/Mg²⁺/Ca²⁺ move fluids, fire nerves and build bones, while trace Fe/Cu/Zn/Ni/Co/Cr catalyse enzymes in milligrams. Chlorophyll is a magnesium porphyrin — no Mg, no photosynthesis. Haemoglobin is an iron porphyrin — no Fe, no oxygen transport. The Na⁺/K⁺ pump burns ATP to hold the gradients nerves fire on; the same metals turn toxic in excess (Pb, Hg, Cd, As) or even iron overload.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: chlorophyll: Mg-centred chlorin (C₅₅H₇₂MgN₄O₅) — Mg deficiency → chlorosis (yellow leaves)  ·  haem: Fe²⁺ porphyrin ×4 in haemoglobin; Fe deficiency → anaemia  ·  Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase: 3 Na⁺ out, 2 K⁺ in per ATP  ·  trace MCQ answer: iron builds haemoglobin (NEB 2022)

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Essentiality is dose-shaped: deficiency cripples, excess poisons (same element, U-shaped curve). Chlorophyll needs Mg specifically — other M²⁺ will not substitute in the ring. Pump stoichiometry (3:2) holds per ATP hydrolysed under physiological conditions.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Mg-deficient soil → yellow (chlorotic) leaves, stunted photosynthesis (NEB 2023). Cobalt centres vitamin B₁₂; zinc fingers grip DNA; copper rides in cytochrome oxidase and haemocyanin. Arsenic groundwater and Minamata mercury show the toxic end of the same periodic table.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Chlorophyll formula centres on Mg²⁺ in a chlorin ring — magnesium harvests light energy into the photosystems; deficiency yellows leaves and stalls growth, corrected by Mg fertilisers like Epsom salt (NEB 2023, 3 marks). The haemoglobin MCQ resolves the same way: iron is the O₂-binding trace metal (NEB 2022).

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: One ion, many jobs — assigning single functions oversimplifies (Ca²⁺ signals, structures AND clots). Soil/plant/animal transfer chains complicate deficiency diagnosis. Toxicity thresholds vary by species, age and chemical form (methylmercury ≫ elemental Hg).

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Why Mg for chlorophyll? Its size and +2 charge fit the chlorin cavity and tune the ring's absorption into the red/blue peaks — photochemistry follows from the metal–ligand electronics. Why Fe for blood? Fe²⁺ binds O₂ reversibly (oxy/deoxy flip) without oxidising — the porphyrin cage protects the +2 state that free Fe²⁺ would lose.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Green plant pigment → Mg; red blood pigment → Fe; nerve gradients → Na⁺/K⁺ pump (3-out-2-in); bones/teeth → Ca/P. Deficiency questions: match the metal to its flagship molecule and the symptom writes itself.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: NEB 2023 (3): chlorophyll formula + Mg's role + deficiency effect. NEB 2022 (1): trace element for haemoglobin — iron (MCQ). Ion-pump stoichiometry and metal-toxicity pairs rotate yearly.
